problem_solving_method: A deterministic TypeScript calculation engine rebuilds the daily meter ledger, projects run-out and target-date recharge needs, and simulates both recharge habits. A React dashboard presents the supplied fixture, calculations, and evidence in one page.

R3.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts:89-220; src/routes/index.tsx:158-195. Includes run-out date, target-date recharge, base energy, slab premium, fixed charges, and VAT.

R4.evidence: src/lib/engine.ts:223-322; src/routes/index.tsx:198-234. Uses identical readings and monthly slab counters and separates consumed cost from deposited money.

major_design_decisions: Use a deterministic engine with calendar-month slab counters so recharge timing cannot create an energy-rate saving.
Separate consumed cost from deposited recharge money to match the evaluation definition.
Keep the public JSON fixture as the reproducible source of truth for judges.
known_limitations: The app uses a static fixture and does not provide data entry or persistence.
Target-date estimates conservatively reserve fixed charges for future months.
